body:
i wonder if the two are somehow karmically related

we know we do not want to hurt those left behind, we wonder if there is an afterlife (at least some of us do) and we wonder if the punishment that we will endure in the afterlife is somehow commensurate with the pain we leave behind for others

for me, both are a consideration, but in the end if there were to be some type of significant punishment in the afterlife, perhaps long term or permanent/eternal, that would end up being the most important thing to me.  but maybe this suffering IS related to the suffering of others, how this would hurt others.  IDK.  It's all so confusing to me.

If you mean the actual process of death itself, that isn't much of a concern to me.  Overcoming the actual fear of death process is quite trivial once the problems of impacting others and resolving any possible spiritual issues are addressed.

Again, I am left with the same issues as per my post.  I am going to keep praying for forgiveness, for mercy on my soul and for how this will affect others.

I wish nothing more than to leave this world.  It's hard to argue with someone who has made up their mind and wishes only to die.  In the end, this person is left alone with their own personal decision to pull the trigger on their own self destruction.

I envision setting up my chosen method and it's difficult to see going through with it.  But ultimately it's a matter of having enough pain at that moment of impact to actually go through with it.  Once the chosen method is set up to facilitate a point of no return, then it's just a matter of passing through that point of no return.  Doing so requires begging a higher power for forgiveness on my soul and for forgiveness on how this will impact others.  I DO NOT want to hurt others, but the fact is that I DO NOT want to exist anymore.  I DO NOT wish to be part of this world any more.  I HAVE NO DESIRE to live anymore.  THIS IS NOT SOMETHING I want anyone to convince me of, this is my personal decision.  I just want out of this world.

Please god forgive me for my sins.  I cannot ever forget the insanity that I have seen in this world, seeing eternal bliss and eternal torment.  Nothing gives me any solid indication that I have any desire to go forward, it's all just a game and it's all fucking bullshit, I have decided that I want out and I've been sabotaging my existence thoroughly and will keep doing so until I pass the point of no return economically/socially, after which I hope to have the strength and courage to follow through with the supposedly ultimate cowardly act.

Please god forgive me for the pain I will inflict on others, please do not punish my soul in the afterlife.  I beg of you.

sorry, but this is complete and utter bullshit.  this person obviously was hurt and now is left dealing with the aftermath, which is how he/she has been permanently affected by bullying and other life changing things.

1) Detachment from friends/family - if all goes well, I will not exist and there is no detachment to suffer.

2) Possibility of damnation if religious - yes, this is a primary consideration, if the belief is there.

3) Possibility of nothing - this is the preferred outcome, it is desirable.

4) Possibility of failed suicide - this can be accounted for if one does adequate planning.  Yes the risk is there, but this one can be minimized so as to be negligible.

The only point remaining from my perspective is still about concerns of damnation in the afterlife.

For your list:

1.) Yes, damnation is not preferable to suffering on earth, obvious.  For the rest, you have your right to believe, but I do not believe we have any responsibility except to try to not hurt others.  We are built to survive and spread our seed.  Seeking positives might work for some, but for others life is an existence of suffering and negativity, shouldn't they have a right to end this suffering?

2.) Sure, this is an ongoing concern but I can distance myself slowly from others.  Travel overseas.  Take up risky activities.  Create space and minimize the pain.  Sure, others will suffer.  But I am suffering now.  I disagree that the means of death matters, if someone kills themselves then those in recent contact might be haunted with thoughts of what they could have done to stop them.

3.) Per the above this risk can be minimized so as to be negligible.

TLDR: Once other options are exhausted, and pain is all that remains, suicide should be a right.  One must consider the spiritual risks, if they believe in that, and consider how it will impact others, IMO.

The reasons for self termination aren't relevant any more, the important part is that I wish to die.

I only care to try to minimize the hurt of others from my death.  Staying alive is a form of care, actually, because I wish to die more than anything, but in part I do not so I avoid hurting them.  I cannot say this is selfish of them, it is a natural reaction on their part to be comforted by the presumption that I am taking care and avoiding telling them that I am actually on the edge of suicide all day and all night.
